label: start
name: starting architecture
last_analysis: All 9 trials scored exactly 0, on dev and in training, across very different heads (pooled, layer-gated, footprint-gather, dihedral, dense FC, per-action attention). So the bottleneck is probably not how actions map to cells. The likely causes are learning speed and precision. An exact build needs roughly 10 to 30 correct placements in a row, then DONE at exactly the right moment, and every run so far had only 32 to 120 policy updates. Recipe space is barely explored: only 2- and 4-epoch runs with 128 or 256 envs. The program says ppo_epochs=1 gives about 3.25x more environment steps, and that is untested. DONE has always been scored from weak mean/max pooling of trunk features. A learned per-cell projection followed by amax could better detect "anything still missing". This last round bets on more samples and policy updates, a sharper DONE and value signal, small-init output layers, and one global-attention variant.
